title: Frobenius preserves an open subscheme defined over the finite field
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber].
Let $j_0:X_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]
of $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base], where $k_0=\mathbf F_q$,
and let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be its base change to $k$ [def-pc-base-change].
Here $X=X_0\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}k$ and
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}k$; write $a_X,a_Y$ for the projections
 to $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-fibre-product].
For $Z_0=X_0,Y_0$, let $F_{Z_0}$ be its absolute $p$-power Frobenius
[def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme], and put
$\Phi_{Z_0}=F_{Z_0}^{a}$ and
$\Phi_Z=\Phi_{Z_0}\times_{k_0}\operatorname{id}_k$.
Thus $\Phi_{Z_0}$ is the $q$-power scheme Frobenius (on sections, $r\mapsto r^q$).
Let $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$
[def-weil-frobenius-substitution], put $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$
[def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let
$g_Z=\operatorname{id}_{Z_0}\times_{k_0}g_s$.
These constructions do not require a finite-type hypothesis.
For each integer $m\geq0$, each square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X&\xrightarrow{h}&X\\
{\scriptstyle j}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle j}\\
Y&\xrightarrow{\bar h}&Y
\end{array}
$$

is Cartesian (in the category of schemes), where
$(h,\bar h)=(\Phi_X^m,\Phi_Y^m)$ or $(g_X^m,g_Y^m)$.
Moreover,

$$
a_Xg_X^m=g_s^ma_X,\qquad a_Yg_Y^m=g_s^ma_Y.
$$

In particular these Galois maps are not asserted to be $k$-morphisms.

proof.text: Write $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. Each structure map to $S_0$ gives a unital map $k_0\to\mathcal O_{Z_0}(U)$ on every open $U$, so $p\cdot1$ maps to zero; hence $X_0,Y_0$ are of characteristic $p$, including empty opens. Identify $X_0$ with its open image in $Y_0$, with restricted structure sheaf, using [def-weil-open-immersion]. By [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme], $F_{Y_0}^{am}$ is the identity on the underlying space and acts by $r\mapsto r^{p^{am}}=r^{q^m}$ on sections. Its restriction to $X_0$ has exactly these same two components, and hence equals $F_{X_0}^{am}$. This gives $j_0\Phi_{X_0}^m=\Phi_{Y_0}^mj_0$ and $(\Phi_{Y_0}^m)^{-1}(X_0)=X_0$. These maps are over $S_0$: [def-weil-frobenius-substitution] states that $c^q=c$ for $c\in k_0$, so the section map fixes the image of $k_0$ on every open. For $m=0$ the same assertions hold with both Frobenii the identity.

source.place: Tag 03SM (definition-absolute-frobenius), with its restriction-of-sections description; explicit q-power iteration

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] to the morphism $\Phi_{Y_0}^m:Y_0\to Y_0$ and the open subscheme $X_0\subseteq Y_0$. By step 1 its inverse-image open is $X_0$ and its restricted map is $\Phi_{X_0}^m$. The cited statement identifies this open, with exactly these restriction and inclusion maps, with the fibre product. Thus the square $(\Phi_{X_0}^m,j_0,j_0,\Phi_{Y_0}^m)$ is Cartesian in the category of schemes; all four arrows also commute with the maps to $S_0$.

First, $j$ is indeed an open immersion: apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to $Y_0\times_{S_0}s$, with open subschemes $X_0\subseteq Y_0$, $s\subseteq s$ and $S_0\subseteq S_0$; the canonical map is $j$. Here is the base-change verification explicitly, using the universal property and functoriality in [def-pc-fibre-product] and the construction [def-pc-base-change]. The model projection of $j\Phi_X^m$ and $\Phi_Y^mj$ is $j_0\Phi_{X_0}^mp_X=\Phi_{Y_0}^mj_0p_X$ by step 1. Their scalar projections are both $a_X$, since $a_Yj=a_X$ and the base-changed Frobenius is the product with $\operatorname{id}_s$; uniqueness for the product proves the square commutes. Let $p_X:X\to X_0$, $p_Y:Y\to Y_0$ be the model projections. Take arbitrary $u:T\to X$ and $v:T\to Y$ satisfying $ju=\Phi_Y^mv$. Put $u_0=p_Xu$, $v_0=p_Yv$ and $t=a_Xu=a_Yv$; the equality of the two scalar maps follows by composing the assumed equation with $a_Y$, using $a_Yj=a_X$ and $a_Y\Phi_Y^m=a_Y$. Step 2 gives a unique $w_0:T\to X_0$ with $\Phi_{X_0}^mw_0=u_0$ and $j_0w_0=v_0$. The latter equality shows that $w_0$ and $t$ have the same composite to $S_0$. Hence there is a unique $w=(w_0,t):T\to X_0\times_{S_0}s=X$. Its projections show $\Phi_X^mw=u$ and $jw=v$. Conversely any such $w$ has model projection $w_0$ by step 2 and scalar projection $t$ because $\Phi_X^m$ fixes scalars, so it is this unique morphism. This is the desired Cartesian property. The descriptions of the iterates used here follow by comparing both projections: $\Phi_Z^m=\Phi_{Z_0}^m\times\operatorname{id}_s$, including $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 01JP (definition-fibre-product); base change of the square verified directly by its universal property

proof.text: By [def-weil-frobenius-substitution], $\gamma$ fixes $k_0$ and has inverse $\gamma^{-1}$. Functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $g_Z^m=\operatorname{id}_{Z_0}\times g_s^m$, with inverse $\operatorname{id}_{Z_0}\times g_s^{-m}$; both product morphisms are defined over $S_0$. Comparing the model and scalar projections proves $jg_X^m=g_Y^mj$. To verify its square is Cartesian, take $u:T\to X$ and $v:T\to Y$ with $ju=g_Y^mv$. Multiplying $jg_X^m=g_Y^mj$ by the two inverses gives $jg_X^{-m}=g_Y^{-m}j$. Then $w=g_X^{-m}u$ satisfies $g_X^mw=u$ and $jw=g_Y^{-m}ju=v$. It is unique because $g_X^m$ is invertible. This proves the required universal property for every $m\geq0$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: product automorphisms; explicit inverse and universal-property calculation

proof.text: For $Z=X,Y$, the second projection of the product map $g_Z^m=\operatorname{id}_{Z_0}\times g_s^m$ is, by the projection identity in [def-pc-fibre-product], $a_Zg_Z^m=g_s^ma_Z$. This proves both displayed structure-map equalities. It is a semilinear equality, and asserts no equality $a_Zg_Z^m=a_Z$; for $m=0$ it reduces to the identity equality.
